references.text: Parallel verses describing the same extent of the plague of frogs in the land of Egypt
The fulfillment of the warning that frogs would come into the houses
The psalmist's poetic retelling of the plague of frogs that God sent upon Egypt
Describes how the frogs swarmed and entered the kings' chambers, a reference to this plague
Revelation uses frogs as a symbol for unclean spirits, with an allusion to the plague of frogs in Egypt
Complementary parts of the same historical event (the plague of frogs) showing God's complete control over nature.
Direct narrative continuation in the same series of plagues; shows the escalation of God's judgment over the same areas.
Theological contrast linked to the Nile: source of a miraculous plague (Exodus) versus source of destruction and desolation (Ezekiel).
